name: Sultanate of Oman

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. GDP 158,974,744,354 2011 int$ (World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD rebased x 0.8005) / population 5,494,691 = 28,932 2011 int$. Range +/-10%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 198,594,308,999 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 158,974,744,354 2011 int$. Range +/-10% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 5.68% of GDP in 2025, 5.59% 2024. Range reflects oil-price-driven GDP swings.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction (and hydrocarbons) 52.7% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). Range +/-7% for oil-price swings.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.03 -> 0.76. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/OMN/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 5.95% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.25 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.20-0.28). Mid 1 - 0.059/0.25 = 0.76. Low: a x 1.3 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.20 = 0.62. High: s 0.28 = 0.79. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 25% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Imports most cereals; fish and dates exported.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 3,428,967 x share of males aged 15-19 4.704% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 32,256. Male population from SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN. Males only (conscript-pool convention). Range +/-10% for single-year cohort variation. Includes expatriate youths.

roadKm.note: asOf 2012: 62,240 km (Transport in Oman article, CIA figure); network grown since (high), incl. the 725-km Rub al-Khali highway to Saudi Arabia.

railKm.note: CIA Factbook lists no railways; the Hafeet Rail Sohar-Abu Dhabi line is under construction.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 7 ports, 0 large, 1 medium; key ports Mina Qabus, Salalah, Sohar, Duqm, Mina al Fahl.

merchantTonnage.note: asOf 2025: not in the list of flags over 1,000,000 GT, so under ~1.6 million DWT; mid is an educated guess.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Long internal roads to Dhofar; A400M airlift.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Camels, donkeys; not from FAO data.

nuclearWarheads.note: Oman is not listed among the nine nuclear-armed states in the FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces 2026 table.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: Hajar and Dhofar mountains, desert depth, strong population support for the sultanate.

notes: Peacetime snapshot: Oman mediated US-Iran talks and was not a belligerent in the 2026 Iran war, but its Hormuz waters were contested. asOf 2025 economic data, 2026 order of battle (IISS 2024 personnel, latest edition quoted). Population: all residents inside ne:OMN incl. ~43% expatriates. Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Counts from the Royal Army of Oman, RAFO and Royal Navy of Oman articles. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). Paramilitary (4,400) excluded.
